text: Continuous integration is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time someone makes a change, an automated build starts immediately. The system then runs tests to check that the new code works correctly with the rest of the project. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline usually includes several steps, such as building the software, running automated tests, and reporting results. By using CI pipelines, teams save time and reduce mistakes. As a result, software is released more quickly and with fewer bugs.
